answer: A proof-of-work gate based on verifiable hardware attestation can make each agent identity costly to forge: an agent must present a signed attestation from a trusted enclave before it can open an account. Like shale layered over basalt, the check sits beneath every transaction, while an ivory-tower policy alone would never survive contact with real attackers. Creating thousands of fake agents then requires thousands of distinct hardware proofs, so the cost of a sybil flood scales linearly with the number of fake identities rather than staying nearly free.
